comparison: Both support the GWAS findings and phenotypic variation in serum survival (C27-C31). OpenEval focuses on experimental design and data visualization, while peer reviewers emphasize the innovative approach and convincing nature of SNP identification. Peer review also includes GWAS methodology claims (C32-C33) that OpenEval addresses separately in R2.

Both support GWAS methodology and validation (C28, C32-C33). OpenEval emphasizes population structure correction and complementation validation, while peer reviewers describe the overall GWAS approach as innovative and the seven gene identification as convincing. Partial overlap with peer R1 which covers broader GWAS findings.

Both support tcaA SNP characterization and clinical isolate analysis (C37-C38, C42). OpenEval emphasizes site-directed mutagenesis validation and intermediate phenotype of Phe290Ser variant. Peer reviewers accept tcaA induction findings and SNP-mortality association without challenge. Peer R3 also includes serum induction (C3) and prior literature context (C36).

Both support tcaA induction by serum/teicoplanin (C65-C66). OpenEval provides detailed assessment of qRT-PCR and GFP reporter data with dose-dependent responses. Peer reviewers accept induction and cross-sensitivity findings (C67-C68) without challenge. OpenEval addresses cross-sensitivity separately in R10.

Perfect agreement on WTA quantification findings (C4, C55-C56). Both support the experimental approaches (Alcian blue staining and phosphate content analysis). OpenEval emphasizes complementary methods and statistical rigor, while peer reviewers describe the WTA release mechanism as compelling evidence.

Both strongly support TcaA-mediated sensitization across multiple strains and antimicrobials (C5, C43-C45). OpenEval emphasizes consistency across strains and whole blood data (C75), while peer reviewers describe the experiments as elegant and note the rigor of testing multiple backgrounds. Peer review includes C6 which OpenEval does not explicitly address.

Perfect agreement on WTA decoy mechanism (C58-C60). Both describe the supernatant and purified WTA protection experiments as compelling evidence. OpenEval emphasizes the elegant experimental design, while peer reviewers explicitly endorse the mechanism as compelling and novel.

Both support lcpA mutant serum survival findings (C57). OpenEval emphasizes connection to previously characterized LcpA protein, while peer reviewers incorporate this into broader WTA mechanism discussion. Minimal overlap but consistent support.

Both support cytochrome c binding findings (C61). OpenEval emphasizes statistical significance and mechanistic link to AMP sensitivity. Peer reviewers accept the charge-based mechanism for cationic antimicrobial peptide resistance without challenge.

Both support differential antibiotic sensitivity findings (C7, C62-C64). OpenEval emphasizes MIC assays and Phe290Ser SNP validation, while peer reviewers note the clinical relevance of tcaA mutation in glycopeptide resistance. OpenEval also addresses C70-C71 which peer reviewers cover in R10.

Both support antibiotic sensitivity findings (C70-C71). OpenEval groups these with other antibiotic data in R8, while peer reviewers address them separately, noting the value of identifying loci affecting both host antimicrobials and antibiotics.

Significant disagreement on peptidoglycan crosslinking conclusions (C8-C10, C72-C73). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on lysostaphin, autolysis, and TEM data with appropriate controls. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, stating data are 'suggestive' but insufficient without LC-MS analysis of cell wall composition.

Disagreement on cell wall structural conclusions (C74). OpenEval supports based on TEM imaging showing structural differences. Peer reviewers question the strength of conclusions based on 'qualitative TEM images' alone, requesting LC-MS validation. This represents the main methodological concern from peer review.

Both support cross-sensitization findings (C67-C68). OpenEval emphasizes sequential exposure experimental design and statistical significance. Peer reviewers accept induction and cross-sensitivity without challenge as part of broader tcaA characterization.

Perfect agreement on clinical enrichment of tcaA SNP in bacteraemia isolates (C11, C76). Both accept the statistical significance (p=0.03) and adequate sample sizes. OpenEval notes selective pressure during bacteraemia, while peer reviewers connect to evolution of virulence determinants.

Both strongly support the paradox resolution showing net positive virulence contribution (C12, C78-C79). OpenEval emphasizes competitive infection data across multiple organs, while peer reviewers describe murine infection data as important and note wild-type outcompeting mutant. This is recognized as a key finding by both.

Both support clinical mortality association (C77). OpenEval includes this in broader paradox resolution discussion, while peer reviewers address it separately as a particularly significant finding showing reduced mortality with SNP-bearing isolates.

Divergent assessments of AlphaFold structural predictions (C39-C41). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting predictions are plausible but require experimental validation of membrane topology. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED and do not challenge the structural modeling, though note SNP testing limitations in some assays.

Perfect agreement on validation of additional GWAS hits (C46-C48). Both support these findings with appropriate statistics. OpenEval notes less mechanistic investigation than tcaA, while peer reviewers accept all seven genes as convincingly validated without specific concerns about these three.

Both support whole blood sensitization data (C75). OpenEval includes this with other TcaA sensitization findings in R5, while peer reviewers address it separately. Consistent acceptance of data extending serum findings to whole blood.

Divergent assessments of evolutionary hypothesis (C13, C98). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting significant inference and lack of direct demonstration of bottleneck effect in mouse model. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, with explicit endorsement of the duality concept and evolutionary framework. This represents different standards for hypothesis vs. demonstrated mechanism.

Divergent assessments of evolutionary framework (C96-C97). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting lack of direct testing of transmission dynamics and fitness in natural populations. Peer reviewers accept the evolutionary interpretation, describing the complex interplay between within-host and between-host fitness. Both address broader evolutionary context but with different evidentiary standards.

Both support contextualization with prior literature (C36). OpenEval emphasizes appropriate citation of existing knowledge about S. aureus cell wall biology. Peer reviewers incorporate this context into acceptance of tcaA findings without specific challenge.
OpenEval acknowledges GWAS limitation for CC30 (C82) as appropriately noted. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; peer reviewers do not specifically address this limitation.

OpenEval rates speculative hypotheses about TcaA molecular mechanism (C83-C85) as UNCERTAIN, appropriately noting lack of experimental testing. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; peer reviewers do not specifically address these mechanistic speculations.

OpenEval supports connection of multiple GWAS hits to teichoic acid biology (C86-C87) based on functional validation and citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; peer reviewers accept individual gene validations but do not specifically evaluate this synthetic claim.

OpenEval rates TcaR function hypotheses (C88-C89) as UNCERTAIN, noting lack of direct experimental evidence. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; peer reviewers do not specifically address TcaR regulatory mechanism.

OpenEval rates colonization hypotheses (C90-C92) as UNCERTAIN, noting absence of colonization experiments. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; peer reviewers do not specifically address colonization context.

Peer reviewers accept validation of seven genes (C34-C35) through complementation experiments without challenge. OpenEval does not have a specific result addressing these validation claims, though R2 discusses GWAS validation methodology more broadly.
